whyEthereum: When batch records sit in a manufacturer's own mutable database, the company being audited controls the evidence and a quality result can be changed after the fact without anyone noticing. Committing each production step onchain puts the record beyond the manufacturer's reach to revise, so regulators and partners get an audit trail that holds because of how it is built rather than because a procedure was followed.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Milestone-based scholarship and grant disbursement
problem: Education grants and scholarships from foundations, governments, and endowments are disbursed upfront with minimal accountability for outcomes — a foundation funding 200 scholarships across 50 institutions has no programmatic way to verify that recipients maintained enrollment, completed required coursework, or met GPA thresholds before the next tranche is released, relying instead on self-reported status updates from institutions that have financial incentive to retain enrolled students regardless of progress.
solutionSketch: Smart contract-governed scholarship funds that release tuition payments in tranches tied to institution-attested milestones — enrollment verification, credit completion, GPA maintenance — with transparent reporting to funders on aggregate outcomes across their entire portfolio.
whyEthereum: When disbursement runs through a single administrator, funders rely on self-reported status from institutions that have a financial reason to keep drawing funds whether or not students are progressing. Building the scholarship fund onchain keeps the release conditions and the record of each milestone and payment verifiable by funders directly, so accountability does not rest on trusting the institution's own reporting.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Mortgage & home-equity rails
problem: Mortgage servicing and secondary market trading depend on legacy systems with slow reconciliation, making loan transfers error-prone and limiting borrower access to competitive terms.
solutionSketch: Servicing and secondary markets become programmable, traceable and accessible
whyEthereum: When servicing and secondary trading run on the private systems of a few large institutions, borrowers cannot see who holds their loan or whether terms were applied correctly, and the records can be reconciled in ways they never observe. Putting the loan and its servicing logic onchain keeps the obligation auditable by the borrower and tradable without permission from a gatekeeper.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Music sync licensing
problem: A filmmaker, YouTuber, or advertiser who wants to license a song for their production must either navigate months-long negotiations with major labels — who often decline small requests entirely — or use generic royalty-free music, because there's no scalable way for independent artists to make their catalog licensable at standardized rates.
solutionSketch: A licensing registry where artists pre-set terms and prices for different use types — YouTube video, short film, TV ad, podcast — so any buyer can instantly purchase a sync license with automatic payment to all rights holders, without negotiation or a licensing intermediary.
whyEthereum: A licensing intermediary decides whose catalog is listed, what a license costs, and when co-writers and producers are paid, and it can hold funds or drop an artist on its own terms. Building the registry onchain keeps the licensing terms and the record of who is owed what with the rights holders, where any buyer can verify a license and payment follows rules no administrator controls.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Open-source contribution records and funding
problem: Open-source contributors build critical infrastructure but have no portable record of their contributions, and funding decisions are made by a small number of gatekeepers disconnected from the people doing the work.
solutionSketch: A portable record of who contributed what to open-source projects, with funding that flows against that record rather than through a handful of gatekeepers. Contributors carry their history across projects and platforms, and any funder can direct money toward the work using the same record, with reward flows that are visible to everyone.
whyEthereum: When contribution history and funding decisions sit inside one platform or with a few gatekeepers, that party decides whose work counts and can deplatform a contributor or steer money toward favored projects. Keeping contribution records and governance onchain lets the people doing the work carry their history anywhere, and any funder can recognize it without a central authority's approval.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Opportunity markets
problem: People with deep contextual expertise — a music fan who spots an unsigned artist, a researcher who recognizes a breakthrough paper, a local supplier who notices a successful business before investors — have valuable information but no institutional connections and no mechanism to monetize their insight. Traditional scout programs can't scale beyond the institution's ability to vet scouts and recommendations. Public prediction markets don't work either: for a scout to profit, someone must lose an offsetting amount — and no market maker wants to bet against thousands of opportunities they've never heard of. If an institution subsidizes liquidity publicly, competitors free-ride on the same signal.
solutionSketch:
Private prediction markets where a sponsor (a label, VC, hiring firm) provides liquidity against outcomes like 'will we sign Artist X?' — but keeps prices visible only to themselves during an opportunity window of roughly two weeks. Anyone can create a market for any opportunity and stake their conviction. As scouts buy YES and drive prices up, the sponsor sees a rising private signal and investigates. If they act and the outcome resolves positively, the scout is paid automatically. After the window closes, positions become public. Designed by Dave White and Matt Liston (Paradigm, August 2025).

Source: [Opportunity Markets, Paradigm 2025](https://www.paradigm.xyz/2025/08/opportunity-markets)
whyEthereum: If the sponsor ran the market on its own system, it would control the prices, the resolution, and the payout, and an outside scout would have no way to know their signal was used or their stake honored. Running it onchain keeps payouts bound to the resolution rule and makes the trades auditable once the window closes, so a sponsor cannot quietly exploit information a scout surfaced.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Outcome-based funding for social services
problem: Large social service contracts — for housing, job placement, addiction recovery — are paid upfront with no enforceable link between disbursement and delivery. Funders have no programmatic way to verify that contracted metrics like bed occupancy, assessment completions, or housing placements were actually achieved before releasing the next payment tranche.
solutionSketch: Smart contracts that release payments to service providers only when verified metrics are independently confirmed — turning outcome-based contracting from a legal aspiration into a structural property of how funds flow.
whyEthereum: When a funder both disburses money and judges whether outcomes were met, political pressure or a comfortable relationship with a provider can loosen the link between payment and delivery, and the public cannot see where the gap opened. Putting the release rule onchain keeps the conditions and the verification visible to everyone, so funds flow against confirmed results rather than a funder's discretion.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Parametric health insurance payouts
problem: Many health insurance claims have simple, verifiable trigger conditions. A policyholder is admitted to a hospital, or completes a covered preventive visit, and is clearly eligible for a payout. These claims still move through the same weeks-long adjudication pipeline as complex cases that need medical review, adding administrative cost and delay to products whose whole value is paying out quickly during a health event.
solutionSketch: Parametric health benefit products where a payout triggers automatically once a standardized medical event is attested, such as a hospital admission confirmed by the facility or a logged preventive visit. Claims that do not need utilization review or a medical necessity determination settle within hours instead of weeks.
whyEthereum: When the insurer alone controls the claims pipeline, it has an incentive to slow or deny payouts on products whose value depends on speed, and the policyholder has little recourse. Encoding the trigger conditions onchain means a clearly eligible event pays out on terms both sides agreed to in advance, without the payer being able to add friction after the fact.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Parametric weather insurance for farmers
problem: Smallholder farmers in climate-vulnerable regions need weather insurance but manual claims processing takes weeks, requires costly adjusters who can't economically serve small policies, and produces disputes that erode trust in the product. Traditional underwriters also reject farmers who lack formal production records, even when satellite and weather data could substitute.
solutionSketch: Parametric insurance products for farmers triggered automatically by satellite imagery and weather station data — when rainfall or temperature readings cross pre-agreed thresholds indicating crop loss, payouts execute without a claim form or adjuster, making it economically viable to serve smallholders at scale.
whyEthereum: When an insurer controls both the policy terms and the decision to pay, a smallholder has little recourse if claims are delayed or denied, and the underwriter has every incentive to stall. Putting the payout rule onchain lets the trigger and the data feeding it stay visible to the farmer, so settlement does not depend on a company choosing to honor it.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Participatory budgeting in local government
problem: Participatory budgeting lets residents propose and vote on how a portion of their local budget should be spent, but the process usually runs through paper ballots, ad-hoc websites, or proprietary platforms that the city pays a vendor to operate. Residents have no independent way to verify that their proposals were registered, their votes were counted as cast, or the resulting allocations actually matched the winning proposals once the budget is later executed.
solutionSketch: A participatory budgeting system where proposals, votes, and final allocations are recorded onchain, with verifiable ballot inclusion using zero-knowledge proofs. A resident can confirm their proposal was registered and their vote counted, the city can show the winning projects tied to actual disbursements, and the connection between what was voted on and what was funded is auditable end to end.
whyEthereum: When a city runs participatory budgeting through a contracted vendor or its own database, the body whose spending is being constrained also controls the record of what residents chose, and any inconvenient outcome could be quietly adjusted or lost between the vote and the budget. Recording proposals, votes, and disbursements onchain keeps the chain from input to execution verifiable by residents directly, so the city's commitment to funding what people voted for becomes structural rather than discretionary.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Patient-controlled health records
problem: Medical records are siloed across hospitals, clinics, and insurers — leaving patients unable to access, control, or share their own health data when switching providers or seeking second opinions. The problem is acute for mental health: a patient switching therapists must reconstruct their entire psychiatric history from memory — medications that worked, dosages that caused side effects, previous diagnoses — because clinician notes have no standard format and no patient-controlled transfer mechanism.
solutionSketch: Systems that give patients direct control over their medical data in a standardized portable format — enabling secure sharing across providers, granular consent over which details are disclosed, and verifiable attestation of test results and clinical findings that can't be silently altered.
whyEthereum: When records sit in hospital and insurer systems, the institution decides what a patient can access and when, and a central store of medical histories becomes a target for breaches and surveillance. Building patient-controlled records onchain keeps consent and access with the patient, lets any provider verify a record was not altered, and avoids routing sensitive history through a company that can log it.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Pay-per-use micropayments
problem: Today's payment rails have an economic floor. Cards cannot profitably process anything below roughly $0.50 because the fixed per-transaction cost eats the margin, which blocks entire pricing models that would otherwise make sense: paying a few cents to read one article, paying per API call instead of buying into a subscription tier, paying per second of video streamed, paying a small tip to a creator. Sellers default to subscriptions, ad-supported content, or steep paywalls because the alternative would cost more to process than it collects.
solutionSketch: Stablecoin payments down to fractions of a cent settle directly between payer and seller, with no per-transaction fixed cost large enough to break the model. Pricing can match the unit of value (one article, one API call, one minute of stream, one model query), and a wallet can authorize small recurring or per-action payments without a card-network preauthorization flow in the middle.
whyEthereum: The fee floor on card payments exists because every transaction is intermediated by networks, processors, and banks that each take a fixed-cost slice. Settling small payments onchain removes that stack, so the unit of pricing can be the unit of value rather than what the rails can profitably process.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Researcher credentials and peer review markets
problem: Academic recognition systems only reward first-author publications, leaving researchers who generate datasets, perform reviews, or replicate studies with no formal credit for work that is essential to science. Peer reviewers perform skilled labor for free on behalf of journals that charge institutions thousands per year — with reviews disappearing after use and no portable track record that follows the reviewer across journals.
solutionSketch: A market for peer review where journals post requests, qualified reviewers bid and are paid automatically on acceptance, and completed reviews become part of a portable verifiable track record — combined with credentials for dataset generation, replication work, and other non-publication contributions that carry the same weight as authorship.
whyEthereum: When each journal keeps its own record of who reviewed what, a reviewer's track record is scattered across publishers who have no reason to share it, and the labor stays invisible the moment they move on. Putting review and contribution history onchain keeps that record with the researcher, readable by any institution, rather than locked inside the publishers that benefit from the free work.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Peer-to-peer energy markets
problem: Rooftop solar owners and other distributed generators have no direct way to sell surplus electricity to their neighbors, forced instead to feed it back to the grid at wholesale rates set by monopoly utilities.
solutionSketch: Local energy trading and microgrids that let participants buy, sell, and balance electricity directly with one another
whyEthereum: A monopoly utility sets the rate at which it buys back surplus solar and is the only party that can match neighbors who want to trade, so it has every reason to keep prices low and the market closed. Running local energy trading onchain lets neighbors transact directly on terms they agree to, with settlement that does not depend on the utility choosing to allow it.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Drug authentication and supply chain traceability
problem: A patient buying antimalarials has no way to verify the drug isn't one of the estimated 1-in-10 medicines in low-income markets that are substandard or falsified — counterfeit drugs with no active ingredient or toxic substitutes kill hundreds of thousands annually. The root cause is that pharmaceutical supply chains lack end-to-end verification from manufacturer to point of dispensing, making it impossible to confirm an unbroken chain of custody at the moment of sale.
solutionSketch: Per-unit identifiers linked to an onchain record of each drug's journey from manufacturer to shelf — allowing any pharmacist or patient with a smartphone to verify authenticity at the point of dispensing, while giving regulators end-to-end supply chain visibility to detect where counterfeits enter.
whyEthereum: A traceability system owned by one manufacturer or distributor can be edited to hide where counterfeits entered, and a pharmacist or patient has no way to check a record the same company controls. Recording each custody transfer onchain keeps the chain back to the manufacturer verifiable by anyone with a scan, so fraudulent insertion cannot be quietly written out.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Physical goods marketplaces
problem: Peer-to-peer resale of physical goods suffers from rampant fraud because there is no trustworthy way to verify item authenticity or enforce payment-on-delivery without a costly intermediary.
solutionSketch: Tokenized listings and escrowed settlement bring transparency to resale and secondary markets
whyEthereum: A marketplace platform holds the funds, decides every dispute, and can favor whichever side it prefers or take fees for the privilege of being trusted. Holding payment in escrow onchain lets buyer and seller transact without trusting each other or a company, with release bound to confirmed delivery rather than a platform's judgment.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Player-owned in-game assets
problem: In-game items, currencies, and progress are locked inside proprietary platforms that can freeze accounts, change economies, or shut down entirely, leaving players with no real ownership of assets they earned or purchased.
solutionSketch: Truly portable items/currency with minimal fees, rentals, AMM-driven markets, escrowed prize pools—shifting power from platforms to players
whyEthereum: When items and currency live on a studio's servers, the operator can freeze accounts, rewrite the economy, or shut the game down, and players keep nothing they earned. Holding assets onchain keeps ownership with the player and lets items move to any game or marketplace that supports the standard, beyond the reach of a single operator's kill switch.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Portable credentials and professional identity
problem: Academic credentials are issued as PDFs locked in institutional databases, skills acquired across employers and platforms exist in disconnected silos, and workers lose their ratings and reputation every time they switch platforms. NGO workers and journalists face the same problem in higher-stakes form: they must repeatedly prove affiliations in hostile environments while sharing full identity documents puts them at risk of surveillance and retaliation.
solutionSketch: Tamper-proof, portable credentials — diplomas, micro-credentials, work history, ratings, union membership, press credentials — that workers and professionals own and carry across platforms, employers, and jurisdictions, with selective disclosure so only the relevant claim is disclosed in each context.
whyEthereum: When credentials live in an institution's database or a hiring platform's records, the worker depends on that operator to stay in business, stay cooperative, and not gate access behind its own terms. Issuing them onchain lets the holder carry proof of their qualifications themselves, disclose only the relevant claim, and have it checked by anyone without routing through a company that can revoke or surveil that access.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Portable ratings & reviews
problem: A review you write on one platform stays there. Your accumulated reputation as a reliable reviewer, the products you have actually purchased, and the ratings you have given are siloed by Amazon, Yelp, Google, and each marketplace, and cannot travel with you to a new app or be carried into a context where the host platform has not approved it. A buyer searching for trustworthy review history on a new platform faces a cold start: the reputational signal is thin or missing entirely.
solutionSketch: Ratings and reviews kept as portable attestations the reviewer signs and controls, with the underlying purchase or interaction proven by an onchain receipt or credential. A reviewer's history travels with them across marketplaces and apps, a buyer can check whether a reviewer actually bought what they reviewed, and a new platform can bootstrap on existing reputation rather than starting from zero.
whyEthereum: When reviews live inside each marketplace, the platform owns the reputational signal and the writer cannot move it elsewhere. Recording reviews and the receipts behind them onchain keeps both with the reviewer, so the same reputation can be presented on any app and a receipt cannot be silently dropped by a platform that finds it inconvenient.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Portable social identity and reputation
problem: Users who build audiences on one social platform lose everything if they switch apps or get de-platformed. Follower counts and engagement metrics are also easily manipulated and impossible to verify independently.
solutionSketch: Onchain handles, profiles, and social graphs that work across multiple apps — combined with verifiable attestations for engagement and community participation that users own and carry with them.
whyEthereum: On a conventional social platform the company owns the follower graph, so it can de-platform a creator or change the rules and the audience does not come along. Holding the handle and social graph onchain keeps the connection between a person and their audience with the people involved, readable by any app, and survivable if one platform turns hostile or disappears.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Clinical trial pre-registration and results registry
problem: Pharmaceutical companies register clinical trials, then selectively publish only the results that support their drug — a practice called outcome reporting bias that systematically distorts the medical evidence base and leads doctors to prescribe treatments that don't work or cause harm, because negative results simply disappear.
solutionSketch: A registry where trial protocols and primary endpoints are cryptographically committed before a trial begins — making it publicly provable whether published results match what was pre-registered and impossible to quietly bury unfavorable outcomes.
whyEthereum: A registry run by an industry body or a single institution can quietly let sponsors amend protocols or delay results, since the same parties that benefit from burying outcomes influence the registrar. Committing protocols onchain fixes the original record where no sponsor or operator can revise it, so anyone can check published results against what was promised.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Procurement
problem: Purchase orders, vendor agreements, and replenishment workflows run through email chains and disconnected ERP modules, with each party keeping its own copy of every transaction. Disputes over terms that were never machine-readable cause delays and duplicate orders. At month-end the same economic event lives as two separate records that have to be manually reconciled, consuming a large share of close-cycle time, and audit preparation depends on weeks of counterparty-confirmation letters.
solutionSketch: Purchase orders, vendor agreements, and replenishment schedules recorded as smart contracts that both buyer and vendor confirm at the point of origination. The same record serves both sides' books, so neither can later claim a different version, routine reorders trigger without manual sign-off, and the reconciliation step at close disappears because the record was joint from the start.
whyEthereum: When procurement and intercompany accounting run through one company's ERP, the terms and the transactions are only as reliable as that party's records, and either side can later claim a different version. Putting the agreement and the transaction record onchain gives both parties the same machine-readable history that neither can revise alone, so the workflow and the audit trail do not depend on trusting one counterparty's system.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Public procurement lifecycle
problem: Government procurement processes are rife with opaque bid evaluations, paper-based contract trails, and limited public visibility, creating fertile ground for favoritism and corruption.
solutionSketch: Transparent record of tenders, bids, evaluations, awards, supplier credentials, deliveries, and payments spanning the full procurement cycle to reduce corruption and enable public audit
whyEthereum: When the procurement record is held by the same agency awarding the contracts, the office with the most to gain from favoritism is also the one that controls what the public gets to see. Recording the full lifecycle onchain keeps bids, evaluations, and payments outside that agency's editing power, so citizens and auditors can check the process without asking permission.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Referral and affiliate payouts
problem: Referral and affiliate programs run inside the company's own systems. It tracks who referred whom, decides which conversions count, and controls the payout schedule. Referrers have to trust that attribution, disputes over whether a referral was credited are routine, and multi-step affiliate chains are hard for anyone outside the company to audit.
solutionSketch: Referral attribution and payout rules encoded so that a qualifying conversion, a signup or a purchase that meets the agreed terms, settles the payout to the referrer on its own. The referrer can confirm their referrals were counted and read the payout rules directly, and a chain of affiliates can each be paid from the same event without the company reconciling every tier by hand.
whyEthereum: A referral program has the company paying people it has a standing incentive to underpay, while also being the only party that records who referred what. Putting attribution and payout rules onchain lets referrers verify their own conversions against rules they can read, so the program does not rest on trusting the dashboard of the business writing the checks.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Regenerative practice incentives
problem: Farmers who adopt soil-building, biodiversity-enhancing, or low-input practices absorb higher costs and risks with no reliable mechanism to measure, certify, and compensate them for the ecological value they create.
solutionSketch: Reward mechanisms that compensate farmers for sustainable and regenerative agricultural behaviors
whyEthereum: When a single program operator records which practices were adopted and decides who gets paid, farmers depend on that intermediary's bookkeeping and funders cannot tell whether the money reached genuine impact. Recording adoption and outcomes onchain creates a payment trail that funders can verify directly and that no intermediary can revise to favor itself.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Reinsurance
problem: Reinsurance capital is locked behind opaque, relationship-driven markets accessible only to large institutional players, with high intermediation costs and no way for cedents or investors to independently audit counterparty exposure or track payout obligations in real time.
solutionSketch: A reinsurance protocol where cedents and capital providers transact directly. Risk tranches are tokenized, payouts settle automatically when a loss event is verified, and reserve levels and counterparty exposure update onchain as positions change. Any participant can audit positions and obligations in real time, rather than waiting on quarterly disclosures and rating-agency snapshots.
whyEthereum: Reinsurance today is intermediated through a small set of brokers, and a cedent's view of a counterparty's book comes from quarterly financials and ratings rather than the live state of its positions. Settling it onchain keeps reserve levels and obligations verifiable by every participant in real time, and lowers the access threshold for new capital providers and smaller cedents to take part.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Migrant worker remittances
problem: A Kenyan nurse working in London sending $200 home loses $12–20 to Western Union and correspondent bank fees — more than the entire daily wage of the family member receiving it — while the transfer takes 1–3 days and requires both parties to have access to physical agents.
solutionSketch: Stablecoin transfers that move value internationally in minutes at near-zero marginal cost, with recipients cashing out through local mobile money networks or holding value in digital wallets without needing a bank account.
whyEthereum: Sending money through Western Union and correspondent banks means a chain of intermediaries that each take a cut, can delay the transfer, and can decline to serve a sender or recipient at all. Moving value onchain lets the two parties transact directly across borders, with the funds staying under their control rather than passing through gatekeepers who price and police every hop.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Renewable project financing
problem: Small-scale renewable energy projects struggle to attract financing because ownership, cash flows, and performance data are not standardized or auditable, making it prohibitively hard to bundle many sites into investable instruments.
solutionSketch: Onchain funding models for solar, storage, and community energy projects that track ownership, cash flows, and performance
whyEthereum: When a financing platform holds the ownership records and reports the performance data, investors depend on that operator's books and it can favor its own deals or fold and strand the projects. Recording ownership, cash flows, and generation data onchain keeps them auditable by anyone, so small projects can be bundled and financed without trusting a single intermediary's accounting.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Real-time reserve attestation for insurance solvency
problem: Insurance regulators assess solvency through quarterly statutory filings that lag reality by months — in the interval between filings, an insurer's reserve position can deteriorate significantly without policyholders or regulators having visibility. The 2023 FIA surplus note controversy showed that even sophisticated state regulators can be caught off guard by rapid reserve changes between reporting periods.
solutionSketch: Onchain attestation of reserve assets that supplements existing statutory reporting — letting regulators and reinsurers see real-time reserve positions between quarterly filings, without replacing the existing RBC framework or requiring insurers to move actual reserve assets onto a blockchain.
whyEthereum: When an insurer reports its own reserves on its own schedule, it controls what regulators and policyholders see and when, so deterioration stays hidden until the next filing. Publishing signed attestations onchain puts reserve positions where regulators and reinsurers can check them continuously and independently, rather than waiting on the party whose solvency is in question.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Residential leasing
problem: Lease management involves manual rent collection, opaque deposit handling, and paper-based renewals that create disputes between landlords and tenants with no neutral enforcement mechanism.
solutionSketch: Lease payments, deposits, renewals and dispute resolution run as smart contracts, eliminating many intermediaries
whyEthereum: In a normal lease the landlord holds the deposit and controls the paperwork, so a tenant depends on that landlord's goodwill to get terms honored and money returned. Running rent, deposits, and renewals onchain fixes the terms in a smart contract both parties agreed to and can inspect, so neither side can quietly change them and disputes resolve against a record no one owns alone.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Revenue bonds
problem: Revenue-based financing lets a business raise capital and repay investors a set percentage of revenue until a return cap, instead of taking on fixed debt or giving up equity. Repayment depends on the business reporting revenue honestly and routing the payments on schedule, so investors fund against numbers they cannot see directly. Enforcement comes down to an audit clause or a lawsuit, which prices small issuers and small investors out of the instrument.
solutionSketch: A revenue-share bond where incoming revenue passes through a contract that routes the agreed percentage to bondholders as it arrives and stops once the return cap is reached. Repayment is a property of the revenue flow rather than something the issuer has to remember to do or investors have to chase, and the outstanding balance is visible to both sides at every point.
whyEthereum: When the issuer controls the books and the bank account, investors in a revenue-share deal depend on self-reported revenue and the issuer's willingness to remit on time. Settling the split onchain makes the repayment rule and the full payment history something both sides verify directly, so a small business can raise this way without investors needing to fund an audit to check the accounting.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Prediction markets for scientific claims
problem: Research funding committees allocate billions based on grant applications reviewed by small expert panels, with no mechanism to aggregate what the broader scientific community actually believes about which hypotheses are likely to replicate, which drugs will fail trials, or which research directions will prove fruitful — leaving funding systematically biased toward incremental work from established labs.
solutionSketch: Prediction markets where researchers stake tokens on the outcomes of specific scientific claims — will this trial replicate, will this drug hit its primary endpoint — with payouts flowing to those who were right. Market prices surface collective scientific belief in real time, and accumulated winnings serve as a credibility signal for funding allocation.
whyEthereum: A prediction market run by one company depends on that operator to hold the stakes, settle honestly, and not exclude participants or views it dislikes, and it can shut the market down when results embarrass powerful funders. Running it onchain keeps the stakes, the settlement rules, and the track record outside any single operator's control and auditable by anyone weighing the signal.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Scientific knowledge graph
problem: Scientific knowledge is scattered across millions of papers and databases with no common layer connecting a finding to the data behind it, the studies that replicated or failed to replicate it, or the retractions that revised it. Whether a given result still stands is hard to see, and cross-domain connections are found mostly by accident.
solutionSketch: An onchain knowledge graph that links papers to their underlying data, their replications, and their retractions, maintained as a public resource rather than inside one publisher's database. A researcher or an application can trace a finding's current standing and follow connections across disciplines without negotiating access.
whyEthereum: A knowledge graph owned by one publisher or database vendor would let that operator decide which findings connect, who can build on the layer, and what gets charged for access, recreating the silos the project is trying to dissolve. Building it onchain keeps the connective layer outside any single institution's control, so any researcher or application can link findings across disciplines without negotiating for permission.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Sourcing records for small-scale producers
problem: A coffee cooperative in Guatemala that practices organic farming can't access premium export markets because the cost of formal certification (USDA Organic, Rainforest Alliance) is $5,000–15,000 per year — prohibitive for producers grossing $50,000. Without certification, buyers have no way to verify claims about growing practices, and the cooperative's product is priced as commodity-grade regardless of actual quality.
solutionSketch: Lightweight, verifiable sourcing records that document growing practices, input usage, and post-harvest handling at the cooperative level — creating a provenance trail that export buyers and roasters can verify without requiring expensive third-party certification as the only trust signal.
whyEthereum: When the only accepted proof of farming practices is a certification body charging fees a small cooperative cannot afford, that body becomes a gatekeeper deciding who reaches premium markets. Recording sourcing claims onchain lets a cooperative build provenance that buyers verify directly, so a track record accrues to the producer rather than to a certifier's private files.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Sovereign & municipal bonds
problem: Issuing and settling government debt involves layers of intermediaries, T+2 or longer settlement windows, and high minimum denominations that exclude smaller investors from participating.
solutionSketch: Onchain issuance, settlement, and coupon tracking of public debt instruments, enabling faster settlement, lower costs, and broader investor access
whyEthereum: The intermediaries that clear and custody government debt set the minimum sizes, the settlement timelines, and the fees, and they decide which investors get access at all. Issuing bonds onchain lets coupons and settlement run on public rules, so smaller investors can hold debt directly and the terms are not gated by the firms that profit from the layers in between.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Spot freight market for trucking
problem: Freight brokers sit between shippers who need loads moved and carriers who have trucks available, taking 15–20% margins on every transaction in exchange for making the match — a spread that exists almost entirely because the broker holds the relationship and information asymmetry, not because they add logistical value that a transparent protocol couldn't replace.
solutionSketch: A spot freight marketplace where shippers post loads with specifications and payment terms, carriers bid directly, payment is escrowed onchain and released automatically upon verified delivery, and both parties build a public reputation from their transaction history — cutting out the broker layer on transactions that don't require physical coordination.
whyEthereum: A freight marketplace run by one company recreates the broker problem: the operator holds the relationships and the reputation data, sets the take rate, and can drop a shipper or carrier from the market it controls. Running the marketplace onchain keeps the escrow and the reputation history outside any one operator's hands, so carriers carry their record between platforms and neither side depends on a middleman to hold funds honestly.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Title & escrow
problem: Real estate closings take 30-60 days and require title companies, notaries, and attorneys to manually verify ownership chains in paper registries, adding thousands of dollars in fees to every transaction.
solutionSketch: Smart contracts replace paper registries and manual escrow flows, reducing settlement time and improving transparency
whyEthereum: Title companies and escrow agents sit between buyer and seller, hold the funds, and are the sole authority on whether ownership records are correct, which adds cost and a point of failure both parties must trust. Recording title and escrow onchain keeps the ownership chain auditable by anyone and releases funds against conditions neither side can quietly rewrite.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Tokenized policies for resale
problem: Insurance policies are illiquid, non-transferable instruments that policyholders cannot sell, swap, or restructure if their risk profile changes, trapping capital and limiting flexibility.
solutionSketch: Policies become tradable contracts, enabling secondary markets, swapping risk profiles and unlocking liquidity
whyEthereum: An insurer that keeps policies non-transferable benefits directly from the trapped capital, and a resale market it operates lets it decide who may sell and at what terms. Representing policies onchain moves the contract and its transfer rights out of the issuer's exclusive control, so a policyholder can sell or restructure coverage without the carrier's permission.
author: Use Case Lab

title: Loyalty points as liquid, transferable assets
problem: Frequent flyers and hotel loyalty members collectively hold an estimated $500 billion in unredeemed points — but those points expire silently, can't be combined across programs, can't be sold, and can be devalued unilaterally by the issuing company overnight with no recourse for holders.
solutionSketch: Tokenized loyalty points that are transferable between programs, sellable on secondary markets, and governed by transparent, immutable issuance and expiry rules — so holders have real property rights over value they've earned.
whyEthereum: When points live in an issuer's private database, the company that owes the value also writes the rules, and it can devalue balances, block transfers, or expire points overnight with no recourse for holders. Issuing loyalty value onchain puts the balance and its issuance rules where the holder can see and move them, so earned value behaves like property rather than a revocable entry.

title: Trade credit clearing
problem: SMEs extend trade credit to each other in isolated bilateral relationships, missing opportunities to net circular obligations and free up working capital that is locked in receivables chains.
solutionSketch: Netting obligations across SME networks
whyEthereum: A clearing operator that sees every firm's receivables holds a detailed map of who owes whom, and it can prioritize certain members, set the fees, or exclude competitors from the netting. Running the obligations onchain keeps the record out of any single firm's hands, so SMEs can net circular debt without handing a private intermediary leverage over their cash flow.

title: Creator royalties for game mods and user content
problem: Modders and content creators build maps, skins, and tools that drive player engagement, but receive no automatic compensation because platforms lack enforceable revenue-sharing mechanisms tied to actual usage.
solutionSketch: Tokenized blueprints, maps or mods permit automatic revenue splits, cross-client recognition, and creator-driven extension of game logic
whyEthereum: When a game platform decides whether and how modders get paid, the company that profits from their work also sets the payout rules and can change or withhold them at will. Putting the royalty logic onchain ties creator splits to actual usage in a way no single platform controls, so compensation does not depend on a publisher choosing to honor it.

title: Urban mobility data networks
problem: Traffic sensors and vehicle telematics data are locked inside proprietary systems owned by individual operators, preventing cities from building a unified real-time picture of mobility patterns.
solutionSketch: Cross-operator sensor and telematics data layers that support traffic optimization, and planning
whyEthereum: When each operator keeps its sensor and telematics data in a proprietary system, every operator holds a chokepoint over the city's view of its own streets and can charge for access or withhold it. Sharing mobility data onchain keeps it readable by any city service without bilateral integrations, so coordinated planning does not hinge on each vendor's cooperation.

title: Water rights trading and usage verification
problem: In drought-prone regions, water rights are traded in informal bilateral markets with no price transparency, while actual usage is monitored by infrequent physical inspections that miss illegal diversions — creating a tragedy of the commons where overuse is profitable and nearly undetectable until aquifers are depleted.
solutionSketch: Tokenized water rights tradeable on transparent markets, with IoT-verified usage continuously recorded onchain — creating a real-time allocation registry where overuse is immediately visible and rights can be transferred without paper title processes.
whyEthereum: If one agency or company runs the allocation registry, large water users can pressure it to overlook diversions or keep trades quiet, leaving downstream users with no independent view. Recording allocations and metered usage onchain lets every rights holder see the same picture, so overuse is visible to the people it harms.

title: Wearables and health data exchanges
problem: Wearable devices generate valuable biometric data that is locked inside proprietary platforms, giving individuals no way to share, monetize, or direct their own fitness and health information to researchers or insurers on their own terms.
solutionSketch: A standard for wearable biometric data, such as continuous glucose readings, sleep stages, or heart-rate variability, where the individual holds custody and grants time-bounded access to specific buyers. Each reading is signed at the device, so a researcher or insurer can trust it has not been altered after capture. Payment for access settles to the individual rather than to the wearable platform, and access ends automatically when the agreed window or condition closes.
whyEthereum: When biometric data sits inside a wearable company's platform, that company decides who buys it and keeps the value while the individual carries the breach risk. Giving people custody of their own health data onchain lets them direct it to a researcher or insurer on their own terms and capture what it is worth.

title: Whistleblower & evidence integrity
problem: Whistleblower testimonies and leaked evidence are vulnerable to tampering, metadata stripping, and retroactive denial, while existing submission channels routinely expose the identity of sources.
solutionSketch: Timestamping and storage of testimonies, photographs, or datasets with privacy-preserving disclosure
whyEthereum: A whistleblower submission channel run by any single organization can be subpoenaed, breached, or pressured into exposing who sent what, and the same operator could quietly alter or lose the evidence. Recording timestamped, privacy-preserving submissions onchain means the source does not have to trust an intermediary that can be compelled against them.

title: Wills and estate execution
problem: Estate execution depends on manual probate processes that take months or years, while trust administration requires fiduciaries to manually manage distributions and reporting across jurisdictions, with beneficiaries having limited visibility.
solutionSketch: Time-locked, oracle-triggered estate execution and programmable trust administration with transparent record-keeping — assets transfer automatically when verifiable conditions are met.
whyEthereum: When estate execution runs through a court, a bank, or a single executor, the people who hold the assets also decide when and whether to release them, and a beneficiary has little recourse against delay or self-dealing. Building the trust logic onchain keeps the release conditions and the record visible to every heir, so distribution follows rules nobody can quietly rewrite.
